data.narrative:
Atom Bodies is a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Tyler Hayes, Doug Satzger, and Eric Monsef, having raised $142.2M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 3 public comparables in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers, though narrow-filter peer matching proved insufficient for statistical reliability.

Of three valuation methods tested, only Stage-Progression proved applicable. This method uses the $142.2M total capital raised as a proxy for current implied value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression to the next financing stage, yielding $284M. Public-Comp Anchoring could not be applied due to absence of target revenue data—standard practice for private companies. Peer-Median analysis was not viable; while 7 same-sector peers exist, filtering by stage, adjacency, and valuation tier returned fewer than the 3 minimum datapoints required for statistical confidence.

The single-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $242M (low) to $327M (high), with a median point of $284M. This range reflects approximately a 1.7x to 2.3x uplift from raised capital. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue benchmarks and limited comparable transaction data for early-stage biotech at this capital level. Additional disclosure of near-term financing milestones or peer transaction terms would strengthen conviction in this range.
